text:
Maya: Quick sync on offer/lease follow-up. We need to nail eviction semantics and fairness before protos land.
Ishaan: Agreed. Two primary concerns: noisy short offers causing churn, and wealthy tenants starving others by auto-accepting everything.
Luis: Proposal: decorate offers with a priority_bucket and a fairness_window. Accepts decrement a per-operator budget; the reconciler enforces per-bucket rate limits.
Maya: I like bucket approach. Also add an opt-in tenant preference: prefer_low_preemptions=true to filter out short preemptible offers.
Ishaan: Eviction timeline: offers -> soft-lease (notice N seconds) -> hard-alloc (if converted)  We need guaranteed notice >= cancel_window or user will see truncated generations.
Luis: Implementation detail: store offer state in intent-store as records: {offer_id, token_count, reserved_tokens}. Keep token_count small (1 per offer unit) to avoid heavy writes.
Maya: On double-accept race: use lease.candidate_token CAS on intent-store. If CAS fails, return 409 with reason claimed. Don't retry client-side; client should poll offer list again.
Ishaan: What about speculative traffic? Tenants can accept multiple overlapping offers to hedge latency. That could double-bill or cause evictions. Need per-tenant concurrent_offers_limit.
Luis: Yep. Default concurrent_offers_limit=2. Configurable per-tenant via account settings. Observability event when tenant hits limit.
Maya: Billing implications: charge a small "hold" fee when token reserved, refundable if not accepted. Then normal usage billing starts on allocation.
tina-bot: note: deploy 4970111111: added metric offer_hold_count and offer_accept_latency to orch-metrics.
Ishaan: For fairness algorithm: simple decay queue. Each tenant has a score; accepting reduces score; time-based decay restores it. Operators can weight scores by SLA tier.
Luis: To prevent gaming, tie score to successful usage (actual GPU runtime), not mere accepts. Otherwise tenant could accept then never use.
Maya: Safety hooks: 1) global headroom reserve (node-level) 2) backpressure to offer generator if offer_reject_rate > 0.2 3) circuit-breaker: if allocation-fail-rate spikes, pause offers in region.
Ishaan: On rollout: start with control-plane-only (offers emitted, but accept returns simulated leases). Step 2: enable real accept for internal tenants. Step 3: canary customers.
Luis: API sketch (JSON):
```
POST /offers/accept { offer_id, tenant_id } -> 202 { lease_id (if claimed) | error: claimed }
GET /offers?filter=prefers_low_preemptions -> list[offers]
```
Maya: UX: Console should show active offers, which tenants accepted them, and expected reclaim_time. Also a stream of offer-revokes for debugging.
tina-bot: reminder: orch-sync today 15:00 — add fairness alg to agenda.
Maya: Action items: Ishaan: prototype scoring decay and limits. Luis: add metrics + intent-store schema. I'll write short rollout runbook and preemption notices guidelines.
Ishaan: I'll park a draft PR for scoring and a test harness to simulate heavy accept churn.
Luis: I'll instrument metrics and a small consumer that filters offers by tenant prefs.
Maya: Good. If we keep limits conservative we can iterate fast without infra surprises. :rocket:
